whatis.intro: Inventory carrying cost is what you pay to keep stock you already own. It covers the money tied up in it, the space it fills and the product lost before it sells. It runs as a yearly rate on average inventory: 27% here, or $35,640 a year.

cards.title: A cost that grows by the week
cards.body: The cost of time on the floor. Every week a case sits, it keeps paying for the money, space and risk behind it.
cards.alt: Plus sign, for the cost of time on the floor

cards.title: Running short has a cost too
cards.body: The cost of running short. A lost sale or a substitution has a price too, so the cheapest stock to hold is not always the least stock.
cards.alt: Minus sign, for the cost of running short

cards.title: Not every case carries $0.50
cards.body: The $0.50 a case is an average across 72,000 cases. The rate rides on what each case cost, so a case of beef carries far more than a case of napkins held as long.
cards.alt: Light bulb, for the carrying cost one case really holds

who.h2: Who uses an inventory carrying cost calculator
who.intro: The people who decide how much dated and dry stock a distributor keeps run it to put a rate on holding it. Whoever signs off on a large buy should know that rate before the order goes out.

look.h2: Each carrying cost rate needs a second look
look.intro: Five rates add up in seconds. Whether each one is honest takes longer. Run through the points below before the 27% steers a buying decision.

steps.title: Only costs that move with stock
steps.body: A lease you pay at any stock level is not a carrying cost unless holding less would free the space. Count it anyway and the 7 storage points read high.

steps.title: Losses priced at cost
steps.body: Value the dump log at what you paid, the same basis as the $132,000. Price it at sell price and the 6 spoilage points come out too high.

steps.title: A normal year in the dump log
steps.body: One freezer failure or recall can swamp a year of spoilage. Take it out, or price it on its own, before it sets the rate for years after.

vos.h2: Where VOS fits in your carrying cost
vos.h3: Dated stock costs least when it sells in time
vos.body: VOS does not price your holding costs or change any of the five rates. Its part is on the selling side, where dated stock goes out. Promos reach your customers by notification and text, and they order by voice in the VOS app.
